body: Stars form when gravity gathers gas within clouds. If the center becomes sufficiently hot and dense, nuclei can fuse there. For much of the Sun's lifetime, fusion converts hydrogen to helium in the core. Energy transported to the surface escapes as radiation.

Mass influences how a star develops. A star like the Sun can expand into a red giant and eventually leave a compact white dwarf. Some much more massive stars undergo core collapse. Some such collapses produce a supernova, and a neutron star or black hole can remain.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: These are illustrative paths for single stars. Rotation, chemical composition and interactions with companion stars can change events and outcomes.
purpose: Explain how stellar properties and observations change over stellar lifetimes.
